angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-01.question: During what period does the eel (Anguilla anguilla) have a statutory closed season in Bavaria, and what minimum size applies outside that period?

options.a: 1 April to 30 June, minimum size 30 cm
options.b: Year-round closed season, no catch allowed
options.c: 1 October to 31 December, minimum size 50 cm
options.d: No closed season, minimum size 20 cm

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-01.explanation: Under the Anlage to §11 AVBayFiG, eel is protected from 1 October to 31 December, with a minimum size of 50 cm. An eel caught during the closed season or below the minimum size must be released immediately and with care.

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-02.question: What closed season and minimum size apply in Bavaria to pike (Esox lucius)?

options.a: 1 January to 28 February, 40 cm
options.b: 15 February to 30 April, 50 cm
options.c: 1 May to 30 June, 60 cm
options.d: No closed season, 45 cm

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-02.explanation: Under the Anlage to §11 AVBayFiG, pike is protected from 15 February to 30 April (spawning period) and has a minimum size of 50 cm.

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-03.question: Pikeperch (Sander lucioperca, 'Zander') and pike share the same closed season in Bavaria. Which period is it?

options.a: 15 February to 30 April
options.b: 1 March to 31 May
options.c: 1 January to 31 March
options.d: 15 April to 15 June

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-03.explanation: Both pike and pikeperch are protected from 15 February to 30 April, when both species reach spawning condition. The minimum size for pikeperch is also 50 cm.

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-04.question: Brown trout (Salmo trutta fario) has a winter closed season in Bavaria. Which figures (period, minimum size) are correct?

options.a: 1 November to 31 January, 20 cm
options.b: No closed season, 30 cm
options.c: 1 October to 15 March, 26 cm
options.d: 15 December to 15 March, 22 cm

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-04.explanation: Brown trout is protected from 1 October to 15 March (matching its typical autumn spawning period) with a minimum size of 26 cm.

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-05.question: Grayling (Thymallus thymallus) is an indicator species of clean, fast-flowing waters. Which closed-season/minimum-size combination applies in Bavaria?

options.a: 1 June to 31 July, 25 cm
options.b: 1 January to 30 April, 35 cm
options.c: Protected year-round
options.d: 1 September to 31 October, 30 cm

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-05.explanation: Grayling is protected from 1 January to 30 April and has a minimum size of 35 cm; the closed season covers its early-spring spawning period.

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-06.question: Huchen (Hucho hucho, also called 'Danube salmon') has a particularly long closed season and a high minimum size in Bavaria. Which statement is correct?

options.a: Closed season 1 May to 30 June, minimum size 40 cm
options.b: No closed season, minimum size 100 cm
options.c: Protected year-round with zero permitted take, like a fully wild species
options.d: Closed season 15 February to 30 June, minimum size 90 cm

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-06.explanation: Huchen is protected from 15 February to 30 June and has one of the highest minimum sizes in the Bavarian species table at 90 cm. As the largest native salmonid it is severely endangered and occurs only within the Danube catchment.

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-07.question: Common carp (Cyprinus carpio) differs from many other Bavarian food fish species in that it...

options.a: is protected year-round
options.b: has no minimum size
options.c: has no statutory closed season but a 35 cm minimum size
options.d: may only be caught with special official permission

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-07.explanation: The Anlage to §11 AVBayFiG sets no closed season for carp, but does set a 35 cm minimum size - it may be taken year-round, but only once it reaches that length.

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-08.question: Burbot (Lota lota), the only native freshwater member of the cod family, has in Bavaria...

options.a: no closed season but a 40 cm minimum size
options.b: a midsummer closed season and no minimum size
options.c: a year-round closed season
options.d: a closed season from March to May and a 20 cm minimum size

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-08.explanation: Burbot spawns in winter under the ice; it has no statutory closed season in Bavaria, but a minimum size of 40 cm.

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-09.question: Lake trout (Salmo trutta lacustris), found in large lakes at the edge of the Bavarian Alps, has which minimum size?

options.a: 26 cm, same as brown trout
options.b: 60 cm
options.c: 35 cm
options.d: 80 cm

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-09.explanation: Lake trout has a much higher minimum size of 60 cm than its subspecies brown trout (26 cm), since the lake-dwelling form grows substantially larger. Its closed season also runs from 1 October to 15 March.

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-10.question: What is the closed season for tench (Tinca tinca) in Bavaria?

options.a: 1 January to 28 February
options.b: 15 October to 31 December
options.c: Year-round
options.d: 1 May to 30 June

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-10.explanation: Tench is protected from 1 May to 30 June (its late-spring/early-summer spawning period) and has a minimum size of 26 cm.

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-11.question: The closed-season and minimum-size rules in the Anlage to §11 AVBayFiG are not nationwide-uniform for every species in Bavaria - some are tied to river basins. What does this mean in practice for anglers?

options.a: Nothing, because all Bavarian waters belong to the same river basin
options.b: For some species, closed season/minimum size only apply within the Danube, Rhine, Elbe or Weser catchments; outside those catchments that species has no state-law protection rule
options.c: River-basin linkage only affects the amount of the Fischereiabgabe fee
options.d: Every individual water body sets its own closed seasons independent of the Anlage

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-11.explanation: The AVBayFiG Anlage assigns closed-season/minimum-size rules for certain, usually rare or regionally-restricted species to Bavaria's four major river basins (Danube, Rhine, Elbe, Weser). Anglers therefore need to know which basin their water belongs to in order to know which species-specific rules apply - huchen, for example, is native only to the Danube catchment and is protected there accordingly.

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-12.question: An angler accidentally catches a pike during the closed season at a water where they hold a valid permit. What are they required to do?

options.a: Keep the fish, since the catch was unintentional
options.b: Release the fish immediately and as gently as possible, minimizing injury
options.c: Stun and kill the fish and hand it over to the fisheries warden
options.d: Keep the fish in a keepnet until the end of the fishing day and decide then

angelschein-bayern-schonzeiten-12.explanation: The closed-season and minimum-size rules in the Anlage to §11 AVBayFiG must be observed regardless of whether the catch was intentional. A protected or undersized fish must be released immediately and as gently as possible; keeping it would breach both the fisheries rules and the principle of fair, ethical angling practice (Waidgerechtigkeit).

angelschein-bayern-fanggeraete-01.question: Which of the following fishing methods is expressly prohibited in Bavaria under §15(1) AVBayFiG?

options.a: Angling with artificial lures in daylight
options.b: Fishing with a hand rod from the bank
options.c: Using electric light sources, explosives, poison or stupefying agents to catch fish
options.d: Fishing with a maximum of two hand rods at the same time

angelschein-bayern-fanggeraete-01.explanation: §15(1) AVBayFiG prohibits, among other things, using electric light sources, explosives, poisons, stupefying agents and firearms to catch fish - all methods that conflict with the principle of fair angling practice (Waidgerechtigkeit) and sustainable stock protection.

angelschein-bayern-fanggeraete-02.question: Snag hooks designed to foul-hook fish outside the mouth, free-drifting lines, net traps, fish gaffs/forks and harpoons are, in Bavarian angling...

options.a: prohibited in principle under §15(1) AVBayFiG
options.b: only prohibited at night
options.c: only prohibited for beginners without a Fischereischein
options.d: allowed as long as they are made of metal

angelschein-bayern-fanggeraete-02.explanation: §15(1) AVBayFiG prohibits these devices and methods because they regularly cause unnecessary suffering to fish (e.g. injuries outside the mouth from snag hooks) and are incompatible with the principle of fair, ethical angling practice.

angelschein-bayern-fanggeraete-03.question: Using live baitfish while angling is, in Bavaria...

options.a: generally allowed if the baitfish comes from the same water body
options.b: prohibited under §15(1) No. 3 AVBayFiG
options.c: only allowed with special permission from the lower fisheries authority
options.d: only allowed when targeting pike

angelschein-bayern-fanggeraete-03.explanation: §15(1) No. 3 AVBayFiG prohibits the use of live baitfish, since this conflicts with animal-welfare and fair-angling-practice requirements - the baitfish would be subjected to unnecessary suffering.

angelschein-bayern-fanggeraete-04.question: Setting up new self-catching eel traps is, in Bavaria...

options.a: generally allowed
options.b: only allowed with permission from the local angling club
options.c: prohibited under §15(1) No. 2 AVBayFiG
options.d: only prohibited on lakes, not on rivers

angelschein-bayern-fanggeraete-04.explanation: §15(1) No. 2 AVBayFiG prohibits setting up new self-catching eel traps, in order to protect the already sharply declining eel population.

angelschein-bayern-fanggeraete-05.question: Under §16(1) AVBayFiG, what is the maximum number of bite points (hooks or hook groups) a single hand rod may carry in Bavaria?

options.a: Three
options.b: Five
options.c: Ten
options.d: Unlimited

angelschein-bayern-fanggeraete-05.explanation: §16(1) AVBayFiG limits a hand rod to a maximum of five bite points, preventing a single rod from effectively functioning as a multi-hook mass-catching device.

angelschein-bayern-fanggeraete-06.question: An angler in Bavaria fishes with two hand rods at the same time. What applies to the combined total number of bite points across both rods?

options.a: A combined maximum of six bite points across both rods
options.b: Each rod may independently carry five bite points, for ten in total
options.c: There is no limit as long as both rods are supervised
options.d: Fishing with two rods at once is prohibited in Bavaria in principle

angelschein-bayern-fanggeraete-06.explanation: When two hand rods are used at the same time, they may together carry a maximum of six bite points combined - not simply five per rod added together.

angelschein-bayern-fanggeraete-07.question: A set-out hand rod in Bavaria must...

options.a: be checked at least every two hours
options.b: be under constant supervision so a hooked fish does not suffer unnecessarily
options.c: be allowed to stay unattended overnight if weighted down
options.d: only be supervised while bait is being used

angelschein-bayern-fanggeraete-07.explanation: Under §16 AVBayFiG a set-out hand rod must be kept under constant supervision, so that a hooked fish can be dealt with as quickly as possible (landed, released unharmed, or dispatched properly) and does not suffer unnecessarily.

angelschein-bayern-fanggeraete-08.question: A fish is accidentally foul-hooked outside the mouth during the fight, e.g. on the back or belly. How should this catch be treated?

options.a: It counts like any other legal catch and may be kept
options.b: It must be killed immediately regardless of size
options.c: It was unintentional, and the fish should be released gently if it fails the closed-season/minimum-size rules or otherwise on fair-angling-practice grounds
options.d: It must be reported to the water's owner before it may be released

angelschein-bayern-fanggeraete-08.explanation: An accidental foul-hook is not itself a violation as long as it was not deliberately produced using a prohibited snag-hook technique. The fish is still subject to the closed-season/minimum-size rules in the Anlage to §11 AVBayFiG and the general fair-angling-practice principle (Art. 1(2) BayFiG); if it is protected or undersized, it must be released gently.

angelschein-bayern-fanggeraete-09.question: A day permit for a specific Bavarian water body imposes stricter rules than AVBayFiG (e.g. only one rod instead of two, a night-fishing ban). What applies to an angler at that water?

options.a: The AVBayFiG rules always take precedence; the permit may not make them stricter
options.b: AVBayFiG sets a statewide minimum standard; the fishing-rights holder or lessee may impose stricter, water-specific rules via the permit that apply in addition
options.c: Permit rules only apply to guest anglers, not club members
options.d: Such additional rules are invalid unless they appear in the state regulation itself

angelschein-bayern-fanggeraete-09.explanation: AVBayFiG forms the statewide minimum standard. Fishing-rights holders and lessees may set stricter, water-specific rules via the day permit or water regulations (e.g. number of rods, night fishing, additional closed seasons for locally endangered stocks) that bind all anglers at that water in addition to AVBayFiG.

angelschein-bayern-schein-01.question: What does Art. 46(1) BayFiG require of every person angling with a hand rod in Bavaria?

options.a: Only carrying a national ID card
options.b: Only membership in an angling club
options.c: Carrying a valid fishing license issued in their own name and proof of the paid fishing fee, to be shown on demand
options.d: Nothing, as long as they hold a day permit

angelschein-bayern-schein-01.explanation: Art. 46(1) BayFiG requires anyone exercising fishing rights under Art. 1(1) sentence 1 BayFiG to carry a valid fishing license issued in their own name plus proof of payment of the fishing fee, and to present these to police, fisheries wardens, or fishing-rights holders/lessees on demand.

angelschein-bayern-schein-02.question: In which of the following cases does Art. 46(2) BayFiG exceptionally NOT require the person's own fishing license?

options.a: Hand-rod angling at a club-leased water
options.b: Fishing without a hand rod as an assistant accompanying a license holder, or fishing in closed waters under Art. 2 Nos. 1 and 2 BayFiG
options.c: Any angling under age 18, regardless of supervision
options.d: Any carp fishing, since carp count as a utility fish

angelschein-bayern-schein-02.explanation: Art. 46(2) BayFiG lists two exceptions from the license requirement: assisting (other than by hand rod) while accompanying a license holder, and fishing in closed waters as defined in Art. 2 Nos. 1 and 2 BayFiG (e.g. sealed-off fish ponds).

angelschein-bayern-schein-03.question: Since the BayFiG reform effective 1 January 2025, children and adolescents may fish without their own fishing license if they...

options.a: have completed their seventh but not yet their 18th year of age and fish in the responsible company of an adult license holder
options.b: are at least 10 years old and hold a separate youth fishing license
options.c: have completed their 14th year of age, regardless of any accompanying person
options.d: present written permission from their school

angelschein-bayern-schein-03.explanation: Art. 47(2) BayFiG allows persons who have completed their seventh but not yet their 18th year of age to fish only in the responsible company of an adult license holder. The separate youth fishing license (Jugendfischereischein) previously required through the end of 2024 was abolished effective 1 January 2025 and replaced by this supervision rule.

angelschein-bayern-schein-04.question: From what age can a lifetime fishing license be obtained in Bavaria once the fishing exam has been passed?

options.a: From age 12
options.b: From age 16
options.c: From age 14
options.d: From age 18

angelschein-bayern-schein-04.explanation: Under Art. 47(3) BayFiG, persons who have completed their 14th year of age and have passed the fishing exam under Art. 48 BayFiG (or an equivalent exam) are granted the lifetime fishing license.

angelschein-bayern-schein-05.question: Besides the lifetime fishing license, Art. 47(1) BayFiG provides for a second license variant. Who is it intended for?

options.a: Only Bavarian angling club members
options.b: Adults who have not passed the fishing exam, e.g. for time-limited or tourist angling
options.c: Only commercial fishers with a trade license
options.d: Minors aged 14 to 18 as a replacement for the supervision rule

angelschein-bayern-schein-05.explanation: Alongside the lifetime fishing license, Art. 47(1) BayFiG also allows issuing a fishing license to adults who have not passed the fishing exam - practically relevant for guests or short-term anglers who want to fish on a time-limited basis without a passed exam; the details are set out in AVBayFiG.

angelschein-bayern-schein-06.question: Which five subject areas does the state fishing exam under Art. 48(1) BayFiG cover?

options.a: Only fish biology and water body knowledge
options.b: Only law and boat handling
options.c: Only tackle and bait knowledge
options.d: Fish biology, water body knowledge, conservation and fisheries management, gear/practice including treatment of the catch, and relevant law (fisheries, water, nature-conservation, animal-welfare and animal-disease law)

angelschein-bayern-schein-06.explanation: Art. 48(1) BayFiG requires adequate knowledge in five areas: (1) fish biology, (2) water body knowledge, (3) conservation and management of fishing waters and fish stocks, (4) fishing gear, practice, and treatment of the caught fish, and (5) relevant legal provisions, particularly fisheries, water, nature-conservation, animal-welfare and animal-disease law.

angelschein-bayern-schein-07.question: From what completed age may a person in Bavaria take the fishing exam?

options.a: Twelve
options.b: Fourteen
options.c: Sixteen
options.d: There is no minimum age to take the exam

angelschein-bayern-schein-07.explanation: Art. 48(2) BayFiG allows taking the fishing exam from completion of the twelfth year of age - but the lifetime fishing license itself can only be issued once the applicant has completed their 14th year of age (Art. 47(3) BayFiG).

angelschein-bayern-schein-08.question: Which authority is responsible in Bavaria for preparing and administering the state fishing exam?

options.a: The local angling club
options.b: The Landesanstalt für Landwirtschaft (LfL, Bavarian State Institute for Agriculture)
options.c: The district office (Landratsamt) where the candidate resides
options.d: The Landesfischereiverband Bayern acting on its own authority

angelschein-bayern-schein-08.explanation: Under Art. 48(3) BayFiG, preparing and administering the fishing exam is the responsibility of the Landesanstalt für Landwirtschaft (LfL), which in practice runs the exam in cooperation with the fisheries associations.

angelschein-bayern-schein-09.question: Anyone wishing to fish in Bavaria must, in addition to the fishing license, also...

options.a: retake the exam every year
options.b: deposit a security bond with the angling club
options.c: pay a fishing fee (Fischereiabgabe) to the Free State of Bavaria and carry proof of payment
options.d: prove they hold liability insurance specific to anglers

angelschein-bayern-schein-09.explanation: Art. 50(1) BayFiG requires payment of a fishing fee to the Free State of Bavaria; proof of payment must be carried. As a one-time lifetime payment the fee may not exceed EUR 400, and the revenue mainly funds the promotion of sustainable, nature-oriented fisheries.

angelschein-bayern-schein-10.question: How is the Bavarian state fishing exam formally structured under AVBayFiG?

options.a: 60 minutes to complete, 60 questions, 12 per subject area, for an exam fee
options.b: A 30-minute individual oral exam with no written questionnaire
options.c: A purely practical test with no theoretical component
options.d: 180 minutes with 200 questions and no fee

angelschein-bayern-schein-10.explanation: Under §4(4) AVBayFiG, the exam lasts 60 minutes and comprises 60 questions, split 12 per subject area matching the five areas listed in Art. 48(1) BayFiG. §5(1) AVBayFiG sets the exam fee.

angelschein-bayern-fischkunde-01.question: Huchen (Hucho hucho) is colloquially also called 'Danube salmon'. Why is that name biologically accurate?

options.a: Because, like Atlantic salmon, it lives in the sea and migrates up the Rhine to spawn
options.b: Because, like salmon, it belongs to the salmonid family, but unlike salmon spends its entire life in the freshwater of the Danube system
options.c: Because it occurs exclusively in the town of Donauwörth
options.d: Because it is genetically related to common carp

angelschein-bayern-fischkunde-01.explanation: Like Atlantic salmon, huchen belongs to the salmonid family, but it is a purely freshwater fish that spends its entire life within the Danube catchment without migrating to sea. It is the largest native member of this family and is severely endangered.

angelschein-bayern-fischkunde-02.question: How do brown trout, lake trout and sea trout differ biologically, even though they all belong to the species Salmo trutta?

options.a: They are three entirely different, unrelated species
options.b: They differ only in color
options.c: They are subspecies/ecotypes of the same species that differ mainly in habitat (stream, lake, sea) and the size that habitat allows them to reach
options.d: Only brown trout is a true fish; the other two are crustaceans

angelschein-bayern-fischkunde-02.explanation: Brown trout, lake trout and sea trout are ecotypes of Salmo trutta: brown trout lives in cool running water and stays relatively small, lake trout migrates into large lakes at the edge of the Alps and grows considerably larger (60 cm minimum size versus 26 cm for brown trout), and sea trout migrates to the sea and can grow larger still.

angelschein-bayern-fischkunde-03.question: Why can pikeperch (Sander lucioperca, 'Zander') hunt successfully even in murky water and at dusk?

options.a: They have a reflective tissue layer behind the retina (tapetum lucidum) that improves vision in low light
options.b: They rely exclusively on their lateral line organ and are blind
options.c: They use echolocation like bats
options.d: They only hunt during a full moon and are inactive by day

angelschein-bayern-fischkunde-03.explanation: Like many crepuscular and nocturnal predators, pikeperch have a tapetum lucidum, a reflective layer behind the retina that passes incoming light back through the photoreceptors a second time, substantially improving low-light vision - the source of the characteristic 'cat's eye' shine anglers see in a torch beam.

angelschein-bayern-fischkunde-04.question: The European eel (Anguilla anguilla) has an unusual life cycle. Which statement is correct?

options.a: It spends its entire life, including spawning, in Bavarian rivers
options.b: It spawns in the Danube and then migrates into freshwater
options.c: It is a purely marine fish that never enters fresh water
options.d: It grows up as a catadromous migratory fish in fresh water (including in Bavaria) and migrates thousands of kilometers to spawn in the Sargasso Sea

angelschein-bayern-fischkunde-04.explanation: Eels are catadromous: they spend their growth phase in fresh water, sometimes for many years, including in Bavarian rivers and lakes, then migrate thousands of kilometers to spawn in the Sargasso Sea. This complex migration is one reason for the species' sharp population decline and the corresponding protective measures.

angelschein-bayern-fischkunde-05.question: What is the easiest external way to distinguish crucian carp (Carassius carassius) from common carp (Cyprinus carpio)?

options.a: Crucian carp has four barbels on its mouth, common carp has none
options.b: Common carp has four barbels on its mouth; crucian carp, which has none, has a deeper, more compact body shape
options.c: Only common carp has scales
options.d: Crucian carp grows noticeably larger than common carp

angelschein-bayern-fischkunde-05.explanation: Common carp carries four characteristic barbels on its mouth, which crucian carp lacks entirely. Crucian carp also has a more compact, deeper-bodied shape than common carp and typically stays smaller.

angelschein-bayern-fischkunde-06.question: Grayling gives its name to a distinct river zone ('grayling zone'). What typically characterizes this stretch of water?

options.a: Still, nutrient-rich lakes with little oxygen
options.b: Highly saline estuary sections
options.c: Moderately fast-flowing, oxygen-rich upland rivers located just below the trout zone
options.d: Artificially built fish ponds

angelschein-bayern-fischkunde-06.explanation: In the classic river-zonation scheme, the grayling zone follows the trout zone and describes moderately fast-flowing, well-oxygenated upland streams and rivers. As a demanding species, grayling is considered an indicator of good water quality.

angelschein-bayern-fischkunde-07.question: What is a notable biological trait of burbot (Lota lota) compared with most other Bavarian freshwater fish?

options.a: It is mainly nocturnal and is the only native freshwater fish that spawns in winter, sometimes under solid ice cover
options.b: It is the only fish that eats exclusively plants
options.c: It can survive extended periods out of water by breathing air like a lungfish
options.d: It lives exclusively in the brackish water of the Baltic Sea

angelschein-bayern-fischkunde-07.explanation: Burbot is the only freshwater fish native to Bavaria from the cod family (Gadidae). It is nocturnal and spawns - unusually for a native species - in winter, often under ice, giving it a distinctive place among native fish.

angelschein-bayern-fischkunde-08.question: Whitefish/'Renken' (Coregonus species), found for example in the Ammersee or the Lake Constance catchment, are typically...

options.a: Predatory fish that mainly hunt other fish
options.b: Plankton feeders of clear, oxygen-rich lakes at the edge of the Alps that live in open-water shoals
options.c: Bottom dwellers that feed exclusively on carrion
options.d: Migratory fish that travel to the sea to spawn

angelschein-bayern-fischkunde-08.explanation: Whitefish are coregonids that feed mainly on plankton and live in large open-water shoals in clear, oxygen-rich lakes at the edge of the Alps. Several species or forms are tightly bound to individual Bavarian lakes and are sometimes rare (e.g. certain Kilch forms).

angelschein-bayern-fischkunde-09.question: The European bitterling (Rhodeus amarus), a small, year-round protected species in Bavarian waters, has an unusual reproductive strategy. What does it involve?

options.a: It builds nests from plant material at the water surface
options.b: It is a mouthbrooder like some cichlids
options.c: The female deposits her eggs via a long ovipositor into the gill cavity of a living freshwater mussel, where the larvae develop in protection
options.d: It reproduces exclusively asexually by budding

angelschein-bayern-fischkunde-09.explanation: Bitterling live in close symbiosis with large freshwater mussels (e.g. swan mussels or river mussels): the female uses an ovipositor to lay her eggs inside the gill cavity of a living mussel, where the larvae develop in a protected environment. Because these host mussels are themselves severely endangered and declining, bitterling populations are threatened too, which is why the species is protected year-round.

angelschein-bayern-gewaesserschutz-01.question: What does the stewardship/conservation duty ('Hegepflicht') anchored in Art. 1(2) BayFiG require of every fishing-rights holder in Bavaria?

options.a: To remove as many fish as possible from the water to avoid overstocking
options.b: To stock exclusively non-native, fast-growing farmed strains
options.c: To maintain and promote a diverse, healthy fish population suited to the size, character and productive capacity of the water body
options.d: The duty applies only to state-owned waters, not to private fishing rights

angelschein-bayern-gewaesserschutz-01.explanation: Art. 1(2) BayFiG attaches a stewardship duty to the fishing right: fishing-rights holders must maintain and promote a diverse, healthy fish population suited to the size, character and productive capacity of the water body in question. This duty applies in principle to all fishing rights, except for closed waters.

angelschein-bayern-gewaesserschutz-02.question: How does Art. 1(3)-(4) BayFiG frame the relationship between nature conservation and recreational fishing?

options.a: Nature conservation always takes absolute priority; recreational fishing can be banned outright at any time
options.b: Fishing must be practiced sustainably, weighing nature and landscape protection against social and economic significance; as a recognized cultural element of the landscape, it may not be blanket-banned at suitable waters
options.c: Angling generally takes priority over all nature-conservation concerns
options.d: The statute is silent on this point

angelschein-bayern-gewaesserschutz-02.explanation: Art. 1(3) BayFiG requires fishing to be practiced sustainably, balancing nature-conservation concerns against economic and social significance in line with good professional practice. Art. 1(4) BayFiG recognizes sustainable fishing as an important cultural element of the Bavarian landscape and rules out a blanket ban at suitable waters, aside from narrowly limited exceptions.

angelschein-bayern-gewaesserschutz-03.question: What characterizes a 'closed water' within the meaning of Art. 2 BayFiG, such as a sealed-off fish pond?

options.a: It is artificially constructed or sealed off and does not allow free fish movement to and from natural waters, which is why most general fisheries rules (e.g. closed seasons) do not apply there
options.b: It is any water body that freezes over in winter
options.c: It is a water that is closed to anglers only at night
options.d: Closed waters are subject to exactly the same closed-season and minimum-size rules as natural waters

angelschein-bayern-gewaesserschutz-03.explanation: Art. 2 BayFiG defines closed waters as artificially constructed, drainable or permanently sealed fish ponds and containers, artificial channels used exclusively for fish farming, and other waters lacking a regular connection to natural waters that would allow fish to move freely (e.g. many gravel-pit lakes), excluding oxbow lakes. For such waters, important parts of general fisheries law, including the stewardship duty and in part the closed-season rules, do not apply in the same way.

angelschein-bayern-gewaesserschutz-04.question: Under Art. 3 BayFiG, who generally holds the fishing right to a Bavarian water body if no special third-party legal relationships exist?

options.a: Automatically the Free State of Bavaria for all waters
options.b: The owner of the water body
options.c: Whichever local angling club is nearest
options.d: Whoever first applies for a day permit

angelschein-bayern-gewaesserschutz-04.explanation: Art. 3 BayFiG provides that, as a rule, the owner of the water body holds the fishing right, unless special third-party legal relationships exist (e.g. historically independent fishing rights). Fishing rights held by the Free State of Bavaria remain unaffected by this rule.

angelschein-bayern-gewaesserschutz-05.question: What does Art. 21 BayWG (riparian buffer strip) regulate, and why is it relevant to anglers?

options.a: It sets the maximum length an angling jetty may extend into a water body
options.b: It bans angling entirely within a 50-meter strip along every water body
options.c: It protects a riparian strip along water bodies from, among other things, arable/horticultural use and the use of fertilizers and pesticides, which benefits water quality and fish habitat
options.d: It exclusively regulates the amount of the Fischereiabgabe fee

angelschein-bayern-gewaesserschutz-05.explanation: Art. 21 BayWG protects a riparian buffer strip in which, among other things, arable and horticultural use and the use and storage of fertilizers and pesticides are prohibited. This protects water quality and therefore fish habitat too - a connection the fishing exam tests under water/nature-conservation topics, even though the provision itself primarily belongs to water law rather than fisheries law.

angelschein-bayern-gewaesserschutz-06.question: Under §11(8) AVBayFiG, fish that were legally caught and would otherwise be keepable may still be released under certain conditions ('catch and release' within a management objective). What is this provision mainly intended for?

options.a: So every angler may freely decide to release all fish regardless of any management objective
options.b: Exclusively for competitive angling
options.c: For table fish the angler simply doesn't like the taste of
options.d: Particularly within management and species-protection programs for endangered species, where the day permit specifies which species may or should be released

angelschein-bayern-gewaesserschutz-06.explanation: §11(8) AVBayFiG allows releasing legally caught fish where this serves the management objective, particularly for endangered species within species-protection programs. The day permit for the relevant water must specify which species this rule covers - a blanket release of every catch, detached from any management objective, is not what is meant, and could even conflict with fair-angling-practice principles if done for purely sporting reasons.

angelschein-bayern-gewaesserschutz-07.question: Fisheries wardens (Fischereiaufseher) in Bavaria are appointed by the district administrative authorities (Landratsämter). What powers do they have with respect to anglers?

options.a: They may only give verbal warnings and may never impose fines or file reports
options.b: They may check compliance with fisheries rules, verify the fishing license, fee proof and day permit, and initiate appropriate action up to and including administrative-offense reports for violations
options.c: They may only inspect the water body itself, not anglers or their catches
options.d: Their powers apply only during the fishing exam itself

angelschein-bayern-gewaesserschutz-07.explanation: Fisheries wardens are appointed under the relevant BayFiG provisions by the district administrative authority (Landratsamt) and receive regular refresher training. They are authorized to check the fishing license, fee proof and day permit, inspect the catch, and initiate the necessary action for violations found, ranging from a verbal warning up to filing an administrative-offense report depending on severity.

angelschein-bayern-gewaesserschutz-08.question: What applies in Bavaria to stocking waters with fish, specifically regarding rare species and catfish?

options.a: Stocking with rare or endangered species requires approval from the competent authority, and new stocking with wels catfish (Silurus glanis) is generally prohibited
options.b: Any species may be stocked without approval as long as it is native to Bavaria
options.c: Only carp stocking requires approval; all other species are unrestricted
options.d: Catfish stocking is expressly encouraged to control prey fish populations

angelschein-bayern-gewaesserschutz-08.explanation: Common, widespread species may still be stocked in the ordinary way; stocking rare or endangered species, by contrast, requires approval, to avoid uncontrolled intervention in sensitive populations. New stocking with wels catfish is generally prohibited in Bavaria, partly because as a large predatory fish it can significantly alter native fish fauna and community composition.
